title: Power Apps: model-driven apps as Business Applications in Work IQ
summary: The briefing's availability, defaults, billing and controls are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft documentation. The App Access table route stops at enabling the control rather than selecting and blocking an application; the accompanying note correctly describes the remaining work.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Power Apps model-driven applications in Business Apps in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Power Apps: Model-driven applications in Business Apps in Work IQ

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for qualifying new public production environments.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Government-related environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Nonproduction environments**: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The previously documented November 2026 switch-on for existing environments has been deferred.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No replacement date is given for enabling existing environments.

claims.claim: The general feature-settings article still lists Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences as Off.
claims.quote: | Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences | When **On**, allows reusable business context [business skills](/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-business-skill-overview) to be used by your agents. | Off |

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ respects the user's existing Power Platform permissions, including environment, app and data access.
claims.quote: Work IQ respects your existing Power Platform security permissions. You can only select environments and applications, view data, and perform actions that your permissions allow.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not grant additional business-data access.
claims.quote: Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: Enabling Work IQ might send data from a FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365 outside the applicable authorization boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: The whole Work IQ MCP server has an availability control separate from Copilot audience settings and App Access.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not state how explicit confirmation works for a Copilot Studio agent running without a person present.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ Business Applications confirmation autonomous unattended Copilot Studio tenant setting. Opened use-business-apps-work-iq and add-work-iq; the user confirmation procedure is documented, but no unattended confirmation behavior is specified.

claims.claim: Create and update enforce writable, required and read-only form-control metadata.
claims.quote: Create and update operations enforce form control metadata, including whether a field is writable, required, or read-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft's troubleshooting guidance says to check whether Work IQ is enabled for a missing environment.
claims.quote: Ask your administrator whether Work IQ is enabled for the environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft's troubleshooting guidance says the app's Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting should be On or Default.
claims.quote: Ask the app maker whether **Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps** is set to **On** or **Default** and the app is published.

claims.claim: The model-driven app must be published after changing its Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Select **Save** and then publish the app for the changes to take effect.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Usage and billing depend on the experience used to access Business Applications.
claims.quote: Usage and billing depend on the experience that you use to access Business Applications.

claims.claim: Costs are tracked by consuming experience rather than a dedicated Business Applications category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ in Copilot Studio uses the Microsoft Copilot harness and Copilot Credits for usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ in Copilot Studio is powered by the [Microsoft Copilot harness](../harnesses-overview), which uses Copilot Credits for [usage-based billing](billing-credit-overview).

claims.claim: A separate Work IQ spending policy is not required in the Copilot Studio experience.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses consumption billing. A separate spending policy isn't required for Work IQ.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: **Copilot Cowork**: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Direct Work IQ calls from coding agents or custom integrations are reported under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: **Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly**: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Work IQ API totals can combine Microsoft 365 productivity and business applications context, rather than isolate Business Applications costs.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.claim: The licensed Copilot Chat scenario is not charged extra as a Work IQ API interaction.
claims.quote: You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.claim: One request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.

claims.claim: Consumption varies with the task's complexity, context and work performed.

claims.claim: Work IQ API consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the environment, model-driven app and business data in their request.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.fix: The printed route is correct but stops at enabling App Access. To give a complete blocking route, use the already-cited general article: set controls[3].ui.path to 'Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled > application > Block' and controls[3].ui.docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/control-app-access-environment. Retain the prose explaining that the feature-specific article gives a different setup sequence.

claims.claim: The maker article labels the app option Microsoft Copilot in model-driven apps.
claims.quote: To enable Microsoft Copilot, set **Microsoft Copilot in model-driven apps** to **On**. To disable it, set the option to **Off**.

claims.claim: Preview workloads are enabled per agent in Copilot Studio through agent > ellipsis > Settings > Work IQ > Preview workloads > Enable preview workloads.
claims.quote:
Open your agent. In the agent designer toolbar, select the ellipsis (**...**), and then select **Settings**.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent was found for the per-agent Enable preview workloads setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Work IQ Enable preview workloads API setting; Work IQ preview workloads API configuration. Opened add-work-iq; results document the designer setting but no API operation for it.

claims.claim: Clearing Business apps (preview) under Sources on the Work IQ tool removes that workload from the agent's Work IQ configuration.
claims.quote: Under **Sources**, review the preview workloads, such as **Business apps (preview)**. Keep the workloads your agent needs selected, clear any it doesn't need, and then select **Done**.

claims.claim: The general Agent 365 article includes Registry in the Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Block route.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab.
3. Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant setting prevents sharing between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse even when an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.claim: The AI-experience access article refers to the tenant setting as business applications availability rather than the default-settings article's full label.
claims.quote: Open the setting for **business applications availability** in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ MCP policy
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy documentation disallows mutation operations by default for Microsoft 365 resource paths.
claims.quote:
Work IQ uses a policy layer to help govern how agents access and act on Microsoft 365 resources.
By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ MCP policy applicability
claims.claim: The cited policy documentation does not explicitly settle whether its mutation default governs Business Applications data.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ Business Applications policy mutation confirmation. Opened policy-governance-mcp and add-work-iq; policy text describes Microsoft 365 resources, while Studio says writes are on by default. No Business Applications-specific policy mapping was found.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent was found for the tenant Business Applications audience setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications data Copilot API settings; Work IQ tenant settings PowerShell Copilot data. Opened default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access; no API or PowerShell operation for the audience setting was documented.

claims.claim: The application update call uses Dataverse's documented PATCH-to-record-URI syntax.
claims.quote: Update operations use the HTTP `PATCH` verb. Pass a JSON object containing the properties you want to update to the URI that represents the record.

claims.claim: Mixed licensing reflects included business-data grounding in licensed Copilot Chat and consumption billing for other experiences.
claims.quote:
**Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat**: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.
**Copilot Cowork**: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.claim: Variable cost is consistent with usage-based billing in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (UBB) charges for consumption rather than simply enabling a feature. Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.
